MGT 409 · AI Foundations for Managers · Final project

PhysioTeam

A six-agent AI team that runs the back office of a solo physical therapy clinic on WhatsApp, so the physical therapist can spend time with patients, not paperwork.
AuthorJose Tronco · jesus.troncovalencia@yale.edu GitHub repohttps://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam · public repo · clone: git clone https://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam Run it (~5 min)pip install -r requirements.txt → put PORTKEY_API_KEY in .env → python run.py → http://localhost:8000. Python only; the React build is committed. Full steps: Appendix A. Live appNot hosted permanently (the course key would be public). A Render blueprint (render.yaml) deploys it in one step. What it doesPatients write on WhatsApp; six agents book, apply the clinic's policies, chase payments, draft every clinical form and doctor report, and report results. The therapist only approves. Demo videoSubmitted with this report (5 minutes), recorded on the tester's own computer: introductions, the physical therapist who tested PhysioTeam on the three pain points and the ~2 hours a day they take, Demo 1 (booking) run by the tester, and the tester's verdict. Demos 2 and 3 are traced step by step in Exhibits 6-7.

Executive summary

  1. A solo physical therapist is also the clinic's receptionist, biller and secretary: about 130 minutes a day of booking, reports and finances by the tester's best estimate, mostly at 8:00 and after closing.
  2. PhysioTeam covers the whole back office, not one task. Six PydanticAI agents with 58 tools handle booking, the 24-hour policy, the waitlist, payments, every clinical form, doctor reports and weekly results, on the clinic's own forms. Competitors cover one or two of these.
  3. The therapist stays in charge, in code. Every booking, charge, document and doctor message is an approval card executed by code; all 9 risks in the register (Exhibit 14) have a defense that passed its test.
  4. It is accurate enough to trust as a first draft. On 30 therapist notes the Clinical Scribe filled 93% of the evaluation form and 94% of SOAP notes; 96% of the numbers it wrote appear in the notes (the rest are flagged).
  5. It is cheap to run. A clinic week costs $0.033 in AI; with WhatsApp fees and hosting, one clinic runs on about MXN 183 a month (Exhibit 12).
  6. The prize: the 8:00 hour becomes a paid consultation (case study, initial estimate, n = 1). For Juliana del Bosque, PT, PhysioTeam frees about 112 minutes a day; her 8:00 report hour becomes about 22 consultations a month, MXN 8,800, net MXN 8,617 after running costs (MXN 4.5 per hour freed).

1 · Solo physical therapists in Mexico lose a working day a week to WhatsApp and paperwork, and empty slots to late cancellations

Who has the problem. Most physical therapists in Mexico practice alone or in pairs. The therapist who tested PhysioTeam runs that kind of clinic: one treatment room, about 25 active patients, three sessions a week each. Everything runs through the therapist's personal WhatsApp, the channel Mexico already uses with its health providers: about 78 million users, roughly 60% of the population (Asociación de Internet MX via DPL News).

How it is handled today. Between patients and at night the therapist answers by hand: prices and therapy differences, the address, "can I come Thursday?", the reminder and its "C to confirm", cancellations two hours before a session, "how much do I owe?", receipts for insurance, invoices through an accountant, a gym video with "can I do this?", a daughter booking both parents. After sessions come the forms: a seven-section paper evaluation, a SOAP note per session, treatment plans, and progress reports when a referring doctor asks. I read three real (anonymised) patient chats and the clinic's blank paper templates to build this list; none of that data is in the app or the repo.

Exhibit 1Where a solo therapist's admin week goes: about 13 hours, most of it outside clinic hours
Note: volumes measured in PhysioTeam's simulated clinic week (27 patients, 140 inbound WhatsApp messages, 40 sessions); minutes per task as in Exhibit 20. The tester's best estimate is about 130 minutes a day (section 6). Source: PhysioTeam simulation, Oct 2026; author's analysis.

What it costs.

  • Time: about 130 minutes a day by the tester's best estimate, including the first hour of every morning (13 hours a week in the author's model): about a full clinic day a week, unpaid.
  • Money: each empty hour is MXN 400-600 lost. The 24-hour cancellation charge is awkward to apply by hand, so it is often waived, and a freed slot is rarely refilled because nobody has time to text the waitlist.
  • Patients: about 70% of physical therapy patients don't finish their plan of care (WebPT); a 2021 PLOS ONE cohort of about 445,000 patients found 73% missed at least one visit (Bhavsar et al.). Reminders, quick answers and follow-up are what keep them coming.
Why it matters. A receptionist costs more than the hours it would free are worth to a one-room practice, so the admin falls on the therapist: either the therapist's evenings or the patients pay for it.

What is genuinely new

  • One team for the whole loop. A patient's first WhatsApp, the booking, the late cancellation and its fee, the waitlist refill, the evaluation, every SOAP note, the plan, the doctor's report and the week's results are handled by six cooperating agents that pass work to each other.
  • Built from a real clinic. The clinic's evaluation and SOAP forms (same sections, same order), prices, policy and WhatsApp patterns. Output files follow the clinic's naming rule (yymmdd_PatientName_Type).
  • Control by construction. Approval cards are executed by approvals.py, never by a model; routine clinical questions are batched for the next session instead of interrupting the therapist.
Honest comparison. Doctoralia has a patient marketplace and Jane a certified EMR; PhysioTeam has neither, and it is not yet connected to a real WhatsApp number (section 7). What it shows is that one small agent team can do the work those tools leave to the therapist, for cents a month.

Exhibit 3Agent architecture: patients only ever hear from Patient Success, after the safety layer; anything with consequences passes through code
Source: backend/agents.py, safety.py, approvals.py, sim.py.
Exhibit 4Roles and tools: 58 tools, most of them deterministic Python the agents call
AgentRoleToolsRepresentative tools
Operations Partner (lead)Chief of staff: agenda, policy, money, patient logistics21get_agenda, move / book / cancel_appointment, block_time, offer_slot_to_waitlist, book_plan_sessions, agenda_outlook, patient_feedback, answer_patient_question
Health Advisor (lead)Clinical co-pilot; the referring doctors' contact16complete_evaluation, update_evaluation, write_soap_note, propose_treatment_plan, progress_data, draft_progress_report, reply_to_doctor, draft_discharge_summary, read_study
Patient SuccessThe clinic's assistant on WhatsApp; always says it is an AI14clinic_info, find_slots, request_booking, join_waitlist, answer_slot_offer, cancel_or_reschedule, save_intake, my_balance, record_payment_proof, escalate_to_therapist
Finance OpsBalances, payments, invoices, weekly numbers, price what-ifs, AI cost7balances, record_payment, request_invoice, business_pulse, what_if_price, ai_cost
Clinical ScribeNotes → the clinic's evaluation form and SOAP notes; empty beats guessed-Structured output: EvaluationDraft (38 fields + ROM, strength, test tables), SoapNote
Imaging ReaderReads study photos and PDFs (vision) after the hidden-text scan-Structured output: ImagingSummary

How they are organised. A keyword router (with a one-call model fallback) sends each message from the therapist to the right lead. Leads call specialists as tools and may hand off to the other lead once per request (a loop guard blocks a second hand-off). Patient messages pass the safety layer and go to Patient Success, which can only read the contact's own records and family (enforced in code). Each run is limited to 10 model requests and 12 tool calls, metered and written to an audit trail. Model: all agents use gpt-6-luna, the course model: cheap ($0.10 per million input tokens, $0.01 cached, $0.50 output), fast and reliable at tool use and structured output, which is most of the work. What must never be wrong (prices, policy, approvals, arithmetic) is code, not model.

What I did to cut cost, and the evidence it did not hurt quality

  • Code wherever a rule is enough. Reminders, "C to confirm", accepted waitlist offers, the 1-5 feedback round, the policy, prices and arithmetic run at zero tokens: 176 of 191 outgoing patient messages (92%) in the measured week. 16 of the 51 story steps cost nothing.
  • Prompt caching. Long stable instructions first, so automatic caching serves 83% of input at a tenth of the price. The A/B (Exhibit 13) produced identical work: 2 bookings, 4 documents, 1 safety block, 0 errors in both arms.
  • Small model, tight loops. One model for all agents, keyword routing before the model router, history trimmed to 24 messages, at most 10 requests and 12 tool calls per run, one hand-off per request.
  • Quality check. With these settings the scribe still fills 93% of the evaluation form and keeps 96% of numbers grounded (Exhibit 15); all 51 story steps pass end to end for $0.028.

6 · Case study, initial estimate: PhysioTeam frees about 112 minutes a day for Juliana del Bosque, PT, and her 8:00 report hour becomes about MXN 8,800 a month

Case study, initial estimate. Juliana del Bosque, a physical therapist with a solo clinic in Mexico, tested PhysioTeam on a recorded call (the demo video) and then gave her best estimates of her own operation. She spends the first hour of the day (8:00-9:00) finishing the previous day's reports, about 5 minutes of every working hour on WhatsApp booking, and about 30 minutes after closing on collections and debts. With PhysioTeam those 130 minutes become about 18 of review (Exhibit 18). That frees the 8:00 hour, which becomes a paid consultation: about 22 a month, MXN 8,800 a month, against about MXN 183 of running cost (Exhibit 19). This is one practitioner (n = 1): her estimates, her 8:00 habit, and demand assumed to fill the slot. The four-week pilot measures all three (section 7).

Method: Juliana del Bosque's best estimates of her own operation, given to the author on 2026-10-26 after the recorded session (not stopwatch-timed), after running the three demos herself on a recorded 26-minute call (the 5-minute demo video is cut from it). Limits: one practitioner (n = 1); the "today" minutes are her best estimates, the "with PhysioTeam" minutes are the author's assumptions; stopwatch timings, her clinic hours and demand for an 8:00 slot: the four-week pilot measures them (section 7).

Reach (illustrative): at least 3,360 physical therapists and related professionals work in Mexico (DataMéxico, physical therapists, audiologists and speech therapists employed, Q1 2026; a lower bound: the survey groups three professions and misses many self-employed therapists); at 41 h a month each, about 137,984 hours a month. Note: weekly volumes measured in the simulated clinic (27 patients); minutes per task are stated assumptions, except the tester's own ~2 minutes per booking message. With PhysioTeam the therapist reads drafts and taps approvals; routine messages need no action. This simulated model is a cross-check: it frees 10 hours a week, against 9 in the case study (Exhibit 18). Source: PhysioTeam simulation; author's analysis.
  • Money: refilled cancellations recovered MXN 1,200 in one week (two slots offered, accepted and booked within a minute, one tap each). Over a month that is about MXN 5,160, on top of the 8:00 consultations. In the simulated week, 176 of 191 outgoing patient messages (92%) went out from code at zero tokens, and no patient message needed the therapist urgently.
  • Time: in the case study the freed 8:00 hour becomes 22 consultations a month (Exhibit 19), and the after-hours finance review mostly becomes evenings back.
  • Patients: every session ends with a 1-5 rating and a "why" stored in the patient's feedback file (40 ratings in the week, average 4.6); low ratings reach the therapist the same day. Reminders and fast answers are the levers against the ~70% plan drop-out the industry reports.

7 · Three things stand between this prototype and a real clinic: the WhatsApp number, real data rules, and a month of measured use

Exhibit 21What does not work yet, and what I would build next

Not on a real WhatsApp number. A · Every number, screenshot and document in this report can be regenerated from the repo with the commands below

A1 · Run the app (about 5 minutes; a fresh install took ~4 min)

git clone https://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam
cd physioteam
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env          # add PORTKEY_API_KEY=...
python run.py                   # http://localhost:8000

Then: Therapist → Stories (5 stories, one click per step) or Free play; Patient to chat as a persona. Each visitor gets a private sandbox; Reset starts over.

A4 · Data provenance

  • All patients, doctors, chats and notes are fictional, written to the real clinic's templates. No real patient data is in the repo or was sent to the model.
  • backend/clinical_history.json (15 patients' evaluations, plans, one SOAP per past session) from tools/make_history.py; 30 sample notes in backend/demo_files/notes/ from tools/make_notes.py.
  • Prices, policy and forms: backend/store.py. Model outputs vary run to run: re-runs give the same order of magnitude, not identical decimals.
